title: `header_timeout` is an idle wait, so a client that sends one header byte at a time holds a connection open for as long as it likes.
text: The four connection waits are all idle waits (`rule:http-server/four-idle-waits-all-finite`), and `arm` re-arms the current phase's deadline on every read that moved bytes (`crates/nvs-server/src/io.rs:309-322`, `:417-421`). For the head that is a slow-loris hole: a request head that trickles in never reaches `header_timeout`, and the server builds hyper's HTTP/1 connection with its defaults (`crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs:2308`). The user decided the design: `header_timeout` becomes a whole-head deadline, fixed when the head starts (at accept, or at the first byte after a keep-alive wait) and not pushed out by progress. The body, write and keep-alive waits stay idle waits. There is no new configuration key and no head size cap, because a proxy owns size, and a connection in its head phase counts against no cap. Closing it means `arm` leaves the head deadline alone on progress, the module doc's clock section (`crates/nvs-server/src/io.rs:46-62`) and `crates/nvs-config/src/default.toml:536-538` say so, and the rule is rewritten as three idle waits and one total, as `rule:http-server/a-streamed-reply-is-bounded-by-idle-and-a-lifetime` already words its own pair.
